subject: Commercial: staged commit incentive ladder and true-up workflow
messages:

Subject: RFP follow-up: pricing structure questions and commit model

Hi Vanessa,

Thanks for the response to section 4 (commercials) in our RFP. Procurement had a few follow-ups specifically around commit mechanics and how overages and discounts would apply across quarters and years. High level questions: 

- Can you summarize how Redwood structures a multi-year staged commit where discounts step down as we increase volume?
- What true-up cadence do you support (quarterly vs annual) and can we smooth overages?
- We also need to understand how prepaid compute credits (if any) interact with token billing.

We're trying to decide between an annual flat commit with true-up, or a staged-commit ladder that adjusts price steps as we ramp. Can you provide a concrete commercial example in writing?

Best,
Alison

Ornate Bank

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>

Cc: rishi.malhotra@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com

Subject: Re: RFP follow-up: pricing structure questions and commit model

Alison —

Appreciate the clear questions. I've attached a focused commercial proposal (Redwood_Commercial_Proposal_Staircase_20261210.pdf) and a draft term sheet (SOW-Term-Sheet_OrnateBank_20261210.xlsx). Below is a short, concrete example and the corresponding operational mechanics so your procurement/legal teams can map to the RFP language.

Executive summary (short):
- Offer: Staged commit ladder across three tiers with built-in step-down incentives when forward-looking monthly average use reaches higher bands.
- True-up: Default quarterly true-up with an optional annual smoothing election (see section on smoothing reserve).
- Overage handling: 15% soft-burst cushion at 1.5x list price, then standard overage rate thereafter; credits applied from smoothing reserve before invoicing overages.
- Compute credits: Optional prepaid GPU-hour credits convertible at a published exchange rate; credits reduce per-token bill at month-end.
- SLA linkage: If latency/availability SLAs are missed above the agreed threshold, we apply a unit-level credit against the following invoice (detailed in SOW).

Concrete example (month / tokens / list):
- Band A (entry): commit 5,000,000 tokens/month at $0.00080/token
- Band B (growth): next 20,000,000 tokens/month at $0.00060/token
- Band C (scale): above 25,000,000 tokens/month at $0.00045/token

Step-down incentive: If the rolling 90-day average monthly consumption reaches the Band B threshold for two consecutive quarters, the Band B rate steps down by 10% for the following quarter (similarly Band C enjoys a 12% step-down). Step-downs are capped to prevent retroactive rebate complexity; they apply forward only.

True-up & smoothing reserve:
- Default cadence: quarterly true-up (standard for enterprise). Quarterly true-up reconciles committed tokens vs actual consumption and charges credits/overages.
- Smoothing reserve: customer may elect a 10% monthly reserve (with funds held as credit) that absorbs spikes. When reserve is elected, overages are only billed once reserve is exhausted. Reserve funds roll forward and are deducted from future invoices.
- Optional annual smoothing: if you prefer fewer true-ups, we can do annual reconciliation and amortize monthly consumption for billing; this requires a larger initial reserve (configurable).

Overage billing mechanics:
- Soft cushion: first 15% beyond the committed monthly volume billed at 1.5x list (discounted by any applicable step-down). This cushion is designed for short spikes and is waived if absorbed by the smoothing reserve.
- Beyond cushion: standard overage at list rate (no step-down), applied monthly and eligible for crediting against future committed increases (per SOW).

Compute credits interaction:
- Prepaid GPU credits can be purchased as upfront compute reservations. Credits are converted to token-equivalent value using a published conversion table (annex B). At month close, token-equivalent of credits reduces token consumption for billing. Unused credits expire at contract end unless rolled under negotiated terms.

Other commercial notes:
- Minimum term: 12 months by default for staged commits, 24 months for step-down incentive lock-in.
- Early termination: pro-rated true-up and remaining reserve returned minus consumption; see SOW.
- Audit & metering: monthly CSV of token logs, plus a monthly reconciliation report.

I've kept this intentionally operational — if you want a single-line CFO-friendly view we can add an amortized monthly invoice schedule. Please let me know which of these options (quarterly true-up vs annual smoothing, reserve percentage, and whether you want prepaid compute credits) you prefer and we'll iterate the numbers.

Regards,

Vanessa —

Thanks for the detailed write-up; very helpful. A couple follow-ups from our legal/finance screen: 

1) Can you support a quarterly true-up by default but allow us to elect annual true-up at contract signature (finance prefers annual to simplify forecasting)? If annual is elected, what's the minimum reserve you require?
2) On step-downs: would Redwood agree to a floor discount for Year 2 (we're asking for a guaranteed 5% floor on step-down across the second year only) to protect continued scale economics?
3) Overages & smoothing: if we choose the 10% smoothing reserve, can residual reserve balances be applied to future increases if we expand to a higher committed band within 12 months?

If you can confirm yes/no and point to the draft SOW clauses, we can move to an internal approval gate next week.

Best,
Alison

Alison / Vanessa —

Thanks — I reviewed. Short answers and what we can confirm in the SOW: 

1) True-up cadence: Quarterly true-up remains the default. We will include an optional election at signature to switch to annual reconciliation. If annual smoothing is elected, the minimum smoothing reserve required is 18% of anticipated 12-month consumption (commercially reasonable to avoid bill shock). We'll document the mechanics in section 3.2 of the SOW.

2) Year-2 floor discount: We can commit to a guaranteed 5% floor on step-downs for Year 2 only, provided the customer remains in the agreement window (12-month minimum) and does not materially reduce committed volumes (>25% reduction vs signed commit). We'll add language that allows for recalibration if usage drops below that threshold.

3) Reserve portability: Yes — residual smoothing reserve balances can be applied to future committed band increases within a 12-month lookback period. The exact math (carry forward versus conversion) is in annex A of the term sheet; we'll add an example table.

Next steps: Vanessa, please push the updated term sheet with the three bullet points above captured. I'll approve the concession at the finance level once the SOW reflects the reserve percentage and the Year-2 floor.

Marissa Cole
